discovery: Conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors, enabling the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson
motivation: The 2013 Prize recognised the theoretical prediction of the Higgs mechanism, which was confirmed by the ATLAS and CMS observation of the Higgs boson in 2012. That confirmation depended on two general-purpose detectors of unprecedented scale and precision. Della Negra and Virdee conceived CMS: a compact, high-field solenoid with a crystal electromagnetic calorimeter and all-silicon tracking, designed specifically to resolve the H to two photons and H to four leptons channels. Jenni founded ATLAS and led it through design and construction. Both detectors had to handle 40 MHz collisions, extreme radiation levels and pile-up, and building them required instrumentation advances that have since shaped calorimetry, silicon tracking and trigger systems across physics. Their foresight made it possible to discover the last missing particle of the Standard Model and to begin precision Higgs physics. Recognising them would honour instrumentation as a source of discovery.
